blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and September 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 54 in June to 53 in September (−1.9%), and it took 25.9% of the city’s 116 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 30 in June to 24 in September (−20.0%), and it took 25.7% of the city’s 35 sales over the period.

The monthly write-ups singled out Scottsdale for detached houses in September (a sellers’ best bet); detached houses in July (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in July (a sellers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in August, September (a buyers’ best bet).

Interior grid lots (the real land stock): single detached houses and duplexes on the residential grid, with strata condos and townhomes concentrated toward the Scott Road / 72–84 Avenue node; OCP Map 2 shows Small Scale Residential and Mixed Residential designations in and around the area. A "land" purchase here is almost always a fee-simple lot with an existing house on it.

Lot character from the bylaw ladder, as stated: single-detached minimum lots run RS1 at 4,000 m² (width 30 m, average depth 30 m), RS4 at 610 m², RS5 at 550 m² or 460 m², RS6 at 390 m² (width 13 m, depth 30 m) and RS7 at 335 m² (width 11 m); duplex zones run RD1 at 836 m² (width 22 m, average depth 30 m), RD2 and RD3 at 4,000 m², and RD4 at 504 m² (width 18 m, average depth 28 m, infill duplex); there is no RD5 zone. These are subdivision minimums for the zones named (zoning bylaw number contested —), not a claim that every lot is that size; the zone for a specific lot is confirmed on the City zoning maps.

Duplex title form is a land question here: a duplex can be strata or non-strata in BC — in a strata the owners own their individual strata lots and together own common property as a strata corporation, while a non-strata duplex has no strata corporation. Confirm the title form for a specific lot through BC Land Title / BC Assessment before pricing or writing.

Servicing: Scottsdale is urban North Delta grid — the research documents City flat-rate utilities (2026 flat-rate utility fee $1,658 for a single-family home) rather than well/septic diligence. Parcel-level servicing confirmations (laterals, off-site works on a subdivision): UNCONFIRMED in the research — confirm with the City for the parcel.

ALR vs non-ALR split, as stated: OCP Map 2 shows no Agricultural designation for this part of North Delta, and a floodplain statement specific to Scottsdale was not confirmed in the sources read; property-level ALR status is a check through the Agricultural Land Commission. No ALR split figure is stated for Scottsdale.
: Stated plainly for the form itself, because duplex/strata confusion is live here: a bare-land strata lot IS strata tenure — Form B / strata fees / bylaws apply to the lot.

Delta Rise tower site, 80 Avenue (Scott Road node): the City staff report for the tower site uses the address 11941 80 Avenue and names the applicant Marshall Mountain Homes Ltd. and Comprehensive Development Zone No.

Scottsdale Exchange TOD Area ground: the 2024 OCP designates a Scottsdale Exchange TOD Area, and the City states Bill 47 requires minimum densities within a Transit Oriented Development Area extending 400 metres from Scottsdale Exchange. Lots inside that line carry a density expectation, not a subdivision — an assembly or rezoning proposal on such ground is documented as a proposal, never as for-sale inventory.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Scottsdale

items.t: Municipality: City of Delta, BC — Scottsdale is the south-east corner of North Delta, along Scott Road at the Surrey border.

Boundaries: the City does not publish a street-by-street written boundary for Scottsdale; the working grid used in research is 72 Avenue south, 84 Avenue north, 112 Street west, Scott Road (120 Street) east — a working grid, not an official boundary. Note the Scottsdale Exchange itself sits on the Surrey side of Scott Road, per the City.
Nearby areas: Sunshine Hills Woods to the west, Nordel to the north-west, Newton (Surrey) across Scott Road to the east.

Search / alternate names: "North Delta" generally; "Scott Road corridor"; "Scottsdale Exchange" (the transit node at 72 Avenue and Scott Road); "80 Avenue towers" for the Scott Road / 80 Avenue high-rise node.

Roads and commute: Scott Road (120 Street) with the R6 RapidBus and Scottsdale Exchange at 72 Avenue; 72 Avenue, 84 Avenue, 112 Street and 116 Street are the internal grid; Highway 91 access is via 64 Avenue / Kittson Parkway. Commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED.
Transit: Scottsdale Exchange is the area's bus hub — routes 310, 312, 316, 319, 322, 329, 340, 364, 391 and the R6 Scott Road RapidBus between Scott Road Station and Newton Exchange.

Schools: School District 37 catchments are address-based, with no middle tier. For the sample address 7031 120 St, Delta, the SD37 School Locator result is Heath Elementary (K–7), 11364 72 Ave., and Seaquam Secondary (8–12), 11584 Lyon Rd.; catchments for other addresses must be checked in the locator. Only Ministry-listed names are used.

Parks/facilities: Chalmers Park, 11400 76A Ave (pickleball, sport courts, sports fields, tennis courts, trails, washrooms per the City listing); Gunderson Park at 7630 117 St. No recreation centre inside the Scottsdale working grid was confirmed; the North Delta Recreation Centre at 11415 84 Avenue serves North Delta, and George Mackie Library is at 8440 112th Street at the area's north-west edge in Nordel.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Scottsdale

items.t: TOD density (Bill 47): the City states Bill 47 requires minimum densities within a Transit Oriented Development Area extending 400 metres from Scottsdale Exchange — work the TOD boundary precisely: two similar lots can sit under different density expectations on either side of that line.

ALR rules (no Agricultural designation shown for this area; stated for any parcel check that finds ALR ground): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha); BC Assessment farm-class thresholds in full three-tier form ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.
Federal non-Canadian purchase prohibition — vacant land: Get advice on the current official text for the specific lot.

Property taxes and utilities: City of Delta 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on balances outstanding after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 2, 2026; the approved 2026 Financial Plan included a 2.9% property tax increase for City operational services; Delta's 2026 flat-rate utility fee is $1,658 for a single-family home — a holding cost on any Scottsdale lot. Area-specific levy notes for Scottsdale: UNVERIFIED.

Scottsdale Exchange is in Surrey. The transit hub the whole sub-area is named around sits on the Surrey side of Scott Road at 72 Avenue, per the City — Delta-side marketing that puts the exchange "in Scottsdale, Delta" is wrong on the City's own statement, and the R6 Scott Road RapidBus boarding area at Scott Road and 72nd Avenue is the corridor's dated transit upgrade.
The detached pace led North Delta on a land-relevant base.

The nearest hospital is across the city: Delta Hospital, 5800 Mountain View Blvd, is in Ladner; the North Delta Public Health Unit is at 11245 84 Avenue — health care for a Scottsdale lot buyer is a drive in both cases.

No shopping centre or grocery store in Scottsdale was confirmed on an official City source (research UNVERIFIED list) — a lot buyer pricing "walk to groceries" from a listing line is pricing an unverified claim; the verified anchors are the Exchange/R6 transit node and Chalmers Park.
Page-statement check for this area. Correct email is jaredgibbons@royallepage.ca.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Scottsdale than in June?
faq.a: In Scottsdale, listings of houses fell from 54 in June to 53 in September (−1.9%); condos and townhomes fell from 30 in June to 24 in September (−20.0%).

faq.q: How big is Scottsdale compared with the rest of North Delta?
faq.a: In September 2026, Scottsdale held 25.4% of the 209 houses listed in North Delta and 33.8% of the 71 condos and townhomes listed in North Delta.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Scottsdale from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 30 houses and 9 condos and townhomes sold in Scottsdale over those 4 months.

faq.q: Who can help me buy or sell in Scottsdale?
faq.a: Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, works across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361 or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: How do I find out which school serves an address in Scottsdale?
faq.a: School catchments are set by address, so use the school district's catchment locator with the exact address. Catchment lines change, so check before you write an offer.

faq.q: Can I buy a bare lot in a Scottsdale subdivision?
faq.a: Land trades as individual fee-simple house/duplex lots on the grid, usually with a house on them.

faq.q: How small can a new lot be?
faq.a: By zone, from the bylaw ladder: RS7 at 335 m² (width 11 m) is the smallest single-detached subdivision minimum; RS6 390 m², RS5 550 m² or 460 m², RS4 610 m², RS1 4,000 m². Duplex minimums run RD4 at 504 m² (infill) to RD2/RD3 at 4,000 m²; there is no RD5 zone. Confirm the parcel's zone on the City maps — and note the zoning bylaw number itself is contested.

faq.q: What can I build on an ordinary house lot under SSMUH?
faq.a: Delta's SSMUH regulations (Bylaws 8394 + 8395, June 24, 2024) allow combinations of single detached dwellings, duplex dwellings, secondary suites, coach houses and garden suites, with reduced parking.

faq.q: Does being near Scottsdale Exchange change my lot's density?
faq.a: Potentially, materially: Bill 47 minimum densities apply within 400 metres of Scottsdale Exchange per the City, and the 2024 OCP designates a Scottsdale Exchange TOD Area. Confirm which side of the TOD line the lot is on before pricing development potential.

faq.q: Is a Scottsdale duplex always a strata?
faq.a: No — the Province lists duplexes as a form strata housing can take, which means a duplex may be strata-titled or not; check the title and strata plan for the specific property. If it is strata (including any bare-land form), diligence runs through the Form B; if not, there is no strata document set at all.
